title: Too, enough, very, so, such
goal: Say how much with too, enough, very, so and such
intro: “Very” makes a word stronger. “Too” means more than you want: it’s a problem. “Enough” means as much as needed, and comes after an adjective. “So” goes before an adjective alone; “such” goes before a noun: so kind, such a kind man.

examples: It’s too hot to go out.
The shirt is too big for me.
He isn’t old enough to drive.
She is such a kind person.

mistakes.right: The food is very tasty! / so tasty!
mistakes.why: “Too” is for problems. For praise, use very or so.

mistakes.wrong: He is enough tall to play.
mistakes.right: He is tall enough to play.

mistakes.wrong: It was so a good day.
mistakes.right: It was such a good day.

ex.q: I can’t drink this tea. It’s ___ hot.
Is the room big ___ for ten people?
We don’t have ___ to finish today.
You look too nice in that dress!
ex.fixed: You look very nice in that dress!

ex.q: She isn't enough experienced for this role.
ex.fixed: She isn't experienced enough for this role.

ex.q: He is so a funny guy.
ex.fixed: He is such a funny guy.

ex.q: The bag is ___ heavy for me to lift.

ex.a: It was such a relaxing holiday.

ex.q: Correct this: “Your cooking is too good!”
ex.y: Praise uses very, so, or really.

talk: Describe your room or office. What is too small or too noisy, what isn’t big enough, and what is so nice about it?
